title: Waveform probe kernel arbiter and MIG fanout scheduler for mixed-sku fleets
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Problem: Our current kernel-selection path relies on static SKU heuristics and per-request token-length estimates, which leads to suboptimal kernel choices when MIG partitions, clock headroom, and recent thermal history vary across heterogeneous fleets (H100/L40S/A10 mix).

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'waveform probe' that performs micro-probes at prefill boundaries to characterize per-slice effective bandwidth and clock headroom, feed that into a kernel arbiter that ranks candidate kernels by end-to-end latency and memory pressure, and add a MIG-aware fanout scheduler that favors slice coalescing when safe. Primary targets: reduce prefill tail latency and minimize kernel fallback events on mixed-sku nodes under realistic token-density distributions.

Success metrics:
- 10-20% reduction in 95th percentile prefill latency on mixed-sku tests (H100-L40S-A10 triage fleets).
- Reduce kernel fallback rate by 50% for requests with token density > 0.6.
- No regression in single-sku latency for homogeneous fleets.

Scope:
- Waveform probe: micro-batched probe that measures effective sustained MAC throughput and observed contention at the start of a prefill window. Runs for <2ms and is cached per-connection for 1s.
- Kernel arbiter: ranking function that combines static fingerprint (model architecture + quant profile) with dynamic probe features (waveform score, thermal headroom, recent NVLink saturation).
- MIG fanout scheduler: decision logic to either consolidate onto adjacent slices (coalesce) or scatter requests, based on fragmentation score and probe output.

Non-goals: full scheduling overhaul, persistent cross-node defragmentation, or changing billing heuristics. This is a runtime-serving optimization only.
comments: 2026-03-01 | Aisha Menon: Initial proposal uploaded. See design notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Waveform+Probe+Design. Added microbenchmark plan and measurement harness links.

2026-03-02 | Rafael Ortega: Spike complete. Ran microbenchmarks on h100-l40s-a10 mixed testbed (fleet-phi-3). Waveform probe adds ~1.3ms median overhead when cached; cold probe ~1.9ms. Probe successful at distinguishing A10 vs H100-slab under NVLink noise. Patch branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148.

2026-03-03 | SRE - Jenna Park: Observability added to runtime: probe.telemetry.{latency,score,cache_hit}. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/waveform-probes. Noticed occasional probe latency spikes correlated with garbage collection on management plane; investigating.

2026-03-04 | Perf - Marin Kovac: Lab perf run 2026-03-04: mixed-sku synthetic load (token-density 0.7) shows 18% improvement p95 prefill when arbiter enabled and fanout coalescing heuristic threshold set to 0.65. Attached benchmark CSV to PR commentary. Plan: tune threshold per SKU mix.

2026-03-05 | Rafael Ortega: Implemented fallback safety net: if probe cache misses > 3 within 10s for a node, revert to conservative kernel choice for 30s. Added unit tests for arbiter ranking function. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148#issuecomment-89234.

2026-03-06 | Design - Priya Nair: Reviewed tradeoffs. Concern about probe-induced jitter for ultra-low-latency customers. Proposal: opt-out flag per-route and default probe TTL of 500ms for routes with p50 < 3ms. Added to PR as config: route.runtime.waveform_probe.mode = [enabled, opt_out, conservative].

2026-03-07 | Rafael Ortega: Integration smoke on dedicated-staging passed. Observed kernel fallback down by 62% on targeted workloads. Noticed increased microbatch packing in coalesced mode — added guard to limit coalescing when microbatching could push memory over 85% on L40S slices.

2026-03-08 | Aisha Menon: Readout prep for eng-all on 2026-03-09. Next steps: thorough regression sweep on homogeneous H100 and A10 fleets, CI perf job to run waveform suite nightly, add canary rollout via Console (route flag rollout 10/50/100). Action items assigned below.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Waveform probe enabled in runtime-1.22 branch with unit and integration tests. 2) Perf test: >=10% p95 prefill improvement on mixed-sku synthetic harness at token-density 0.7. 3) No >5% regression in homogeneous H100 p95. 4) Flag to opt out per-route implemented and documented.
notes: Experiment logs and CSVs are stored in the drive folder. We should coordinate with Capacity for canary nodes to avoid interfering with Dedicated customer SLAs. Consider shipping the feature behind a feature flag 'waveform-arbiter' and gating by release runtime-1.22.
